set.approach: Rock Springs Buttress is reached from the Jackson Hole ski area: park in the upper lot behind the lodge, hike the paved road toward the Union Pass lift, take the small trail that leaves to the left where the road ends, then turn left onto the service road, which steepens into a trail up to the buttress. From the top of the tram a cairned climbers' trail descends from the ridge into the base area instead. The route is on the Central Sector, the part of the cliff with the tallest multi-pitch lines, between Crucify the Dread on its left and Red, Green and Gold on its right. A large loose gully separates this sector from the smaller West Sector.

review.notes: Route page places the line between two named neighbours; sector page and main crag page give the access. No descent stated.

set.approach: Rock Springs Buttress is reached from the Jackson Hole ski area: park in the upper lot behind the lodge, hike the paved road toward the Union Pass lift, take the small trail that leaves to the left where the road ends, then turn left onto the service road, which steepens into a trail up to the buttress. From the top of the tram a cairned climbers' trail descends from the ridge into the base area instead. The line is a variation on the top of the route XM on the Central Sector: it follows XM to the last bolt before the final roof, then breaks left to a thin crack, pulls the roof beside the arete, and follows the arete to the anchors.

review.notes: Route page: variation on the upper section of XM; crag pages give the access.

set.approach: Start at the Leigh Lake parking area and walk the trail northward, then pick up the signs pointing to the Leigh Lake portage. Boulder Island sits just offshore, a short swim from the lake edge, or a paddle across from the same trailhead. The route is on the west side of the main boulder, following the clear finger crack immediately to the right of the black dike.

review.notes: Island page gives the access; route page gives the west-side start by the dike. No descent stated for this route.

set.approach: The route is in Boy Scout Cirque in Teton Canyon, at the far right side of the cirque, beyond the Boy Scout couloir and the big roof dihedrals. It follows a diagonal crack to a left-facing dihedral.
set.descent_text: Descend by rappel from the sling anchors at the top of the climb.

review.notes: Route page places the line and says the descent is made from sling anchors with a single rope; rope length left out. Crag page is empty.

set.approach: Rock Springs Buttress is reached from the Jackson Hole ski area: park in the upper lot behind the lodge, hike the paved road toward the Union Pass lift, take the small trail that leaves to the left where the road ends, then turn left onto the service road, which steepens into a trail up to the buttress. From the top of the tram a cairned climbers' trail descends from the ridge into the base area instead. The East Sector is the first part of the cliff reached from below: from the talus under the Central Sector, contour right (east), or take the faint trail that branches right once inside Rock Springs Canyon. From the tram top, pass the West Sector and keep along the base of the Central Sector beyond the big slab. This line is the upper part of For Pete's Sake, normally reached by climbing the lower pitches of Swordfish Lipstick.

review.notes: Sector page gives the access; route page says its upper section is reached via Swordfish Lipstick.

set.approach: Cascade Canyon is reached by the short boat ride across Jenny Lake or on foot around the lake, then the horse trail that joins the main canyon trail. Follow the Guide's Wall approach trail until it approaches the foot of Storm Point's steep south face, then leave the trail and scramble steep, somewhat loose fourth-class ledges to the base of the route. The arching roof of Bat Attack Crack is the landmark; the first pitch of Chilly Dogs, which is Hot Dogs, follows the crack that exits right before that roof, from a ledge shared with Vieux Guide.
set.descent_text: From the top, traverse the exposed ledge west to a large tree with slings and rappel from it, then continue down a fixed anchor to join the rappel line of Guide's Wall, and further rappels off trees and fixed anchors reach the ground; a scramble east leads back to the approach trail.

review.notes: Route page has both the approach scramble and the full descent. Rappel counts left out.

set.approach: Cascade Canyon is reached by the short boat ride across Jenny Lake or on foot around the lake, then the horse trail that joins the main canyon trail. The route begins beneath the obvious Bat Attack Crack: easy slabs and a trough lead to the right side of the arching roof, where this line breaks out right around the roof, sharing that start.
set.descent_text: Walk the ramp that traverses left to the comfortable ledge at the top of the pitch and rappel from the fixed anchor there back to the ground.

review.notes: Route page: start under Bat Attack Crack and a fixed rappel anchor at the ledge. Rappel length left out.

set.approach: Cascade Canyon is reached by the short boat ride across Jenny Lake or on foot around the lake, then the horse trail that joins the main canyon trail. Baxter's Pinnacle is only a short walk up the trail before the turn-off. The route is a variation on the first pitch of the Baxter's Pinnacle South Ridge: it starts right below the first tree on the fourth-class approach scramble, partway up from the base, on a steep, thin orange slab just north of the standard line.

review.notes: Route page places the start; canyon page gives the walk. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the Death Canyon trailhead (reached by the Moose-Wilson road and a dirt road off it), hike past Phelps Lake and up Death Canyon, passing below The Snaz, Caveat Emptor and Aerial Boundaries. Once beyond the last switchbacks on the lower trail the route is easy to spot: the single full-height dihedral cutting the west side of Cathedral Rock. Follow the loose gully that runs beneath the west face; the climb starts a little higher than the lower end of the steep, fourth-class gully used to descend from The Snaz.
set.descent_text: Descend by the Snaz walk-off: the descent chimneys and gully to the south of the buttress.

review.notes: Route page gives approach and the Snaz descent; crag page gives the trailhead.

set.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The line is on Sumac Point's northern end, facing southwest, and lies off to the left as you climb into the cirque.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The line aims at the prominent dihedral high on Sunset Buttress. The lower part of the buttress is easy, unprotectable slab and broken ground with many ways up to a grassy platform at the foot of a right-facing corner, which can also be reached by walking in from the right.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The wall is among the first on your left when entering the cirque: Sumac Point's far-left wall, to the right of Bo Mambo. Walk up the ramp from camp, passing Forest Creatures, until you reach the wall's foot; the start is right of the conspicuous tree.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The route is just right of Martian Moonbase on the lower part of Sumac Point. Take the third-class ledge to the tree, then from the right side of that ledge climb toward the open-book feature and the large chimney above.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: The Cirque of the Moon sits on the south side of the Popo Agie's North Fork. It is entered from Dickinson Park on the Shoshone National Forest roads north of Lander, following the trail down to the river and up through forest onto the boulder floor of the cirque, or by the longer way through the Cirque of the Towers from the Big Sandy trailhead. The route lies on North Sumac Point's southwest side, a little right of Brokeback Mountain. Start at the base of the wall beside the boulders where the rubble pile heads up into the gully, and aim for the left base of the crack that emerges from the apex of the prominent arch.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: The Cirque of the Sun is a small cirque just south of Monolith Cirque. Hike in from Dickinson Park, outside Lander, along the North Fork trail; the final climb into the cirque is brief but steep, and inside it the walls are simple to reach. The route starts just left of the start of Solar Winds.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: The Cirque of the Sun is a small cirque just south of Monolith Cirque, reached by the North Fork trail that starts at Dickinson Park near Lander. The route sits on the way in to Icarus. Find a tall column standing apart from the buttress with a big boulder beside it on the right, and start in the gap between them.
set.descent_text: Every belay carries fixed hardware for rappelling the route, as far up as the crux pitch.

review.notes: Route page: fixed belay hardware for rappelling up to the crux pitch; rope length left out. Name says 5.12- A0, stored grade 5.13- (page lists 5.13-/5.12- A0 with a bypass).

set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows parking lot, follow the Lupine Meadows trail to the junction with the Surprise and Amphitheater Lakes trail, pass Surprise Lake to the camping area, and head north between the two lakes until Delta Lake comes into view. Follow the cliff band that runs east along the south side of Delta Lake. The route is on a west-facing slab where the cliff noticeably juts out, near two spruce trees with gnarled roots; the base is reached by scrambling down or rappelling in.

review.notes: Cliff page gives the access; route page marks the slab. No descent stated for this route.

set.approach: Drive Highway 16 west from Buffalo, turn right at the Hunter Creek Trailhead sign, take the left fork onto Forest Service Road 391 (rocky; high clearance is recommended) and park at the Enormodome camp, just right of the road at the edge of a large meadow. A faint path leads north from camp to a cattle trail heading northeast; leave it to skirt the boggy meadow on its north side, and a cleared path through the young forest runs straight to the south prow of the dome. The East Face is on the east flank of the fin. This route starts just left of the old buck-rail fence that meets the wall, immediately left of Task Force Master.
set.descent_text: Lower off the clip-and-lower anchors at the top, which it shares with Task Force Master.

review.notes: Route page gives the start and shared lowering anchors; crag page gives the access and notes the hardware is for lowering.

review.notes: Route page: shared start with On the Fence and clip-and-lower anchors.

set.approach: The East Fork Road area is BLM land in the East Fork drainage near Dubois. The crack line lies down the hill from Welcome to Dubois, in a canyon with rock outcrops on both sides, below a ranch gate at the top of the hill on East Fork Road. It is reached by rappelling into the canyon.

review.notes: Route page: rappel into the canyon, down the hill from Welcome to Dubois. Location of the gate from the neighbouring route page, used for approach only.

set.approach: The East Fork Road area is BLM land in the East Fork drainage near Dubois. Keep following East Fork Road past the Bear Creek Road turn-off to a ranch gate at the top of a hill, with a canyon below and rock outcrops on both sides. The climb is reached by building a rappel station at the top and rappelling in.

review.notes: Route page gives the gate and canyon; rappel in.

set.approach: Follow the Dry Horse Creek trail up to the saddle that divides Dry from Wet Horse Creek, then follow the ridge southwest through mountain mahogany to the base of the tower. Ledge systems on either side make it easy to traverse around the tower. The route is on the southwest side of the Eocene tower and begins in the left-hand corner, on the rock bridge's south side, where it links the Eocene with Brokeback.
set.descent_text: Rappel the southwest face from the summit, using an intermediate anchor partway down before the last rappel to the ground.

review.notes: Route page: start and southwest-face rappels; tower page: trail and ridge approach. Rappel counts left out.

set.approach: False Rock is a rock pillar in the Bighorn Basin. Take the two-track road to the foot of the mountain, follow the bottom of the canyon until you are close to the tower, then take the draw on the left side of the tower. The route is on the north side of the rock, beside the big crack.

review.notes: Crag page: two-track and draw approach; route page: north side by the big crack.

set.approach: This is a small practice boulder in the Meadows camping zone of Garnet Canyon, the first thing on the left (south) as you enter the zone, on the east side near the crossing of the north fork. The west-facing slab is the practice surface.

review.notes: Route page only; crag page empty.

set.approach: The Ice Cream Cone is a spire just east of the South Teton on the ridge that runs to Cloudveil Dome. It is reached from the west by the South Teton's east face, or from the east via Cloudveil Dome and neighbouring peaks; approaching it directly is not practical because of loose rock and rockfall. The route begins in the col where the Cone meets the South Teton's east ridge, up the evident dark chimney or wide crack that has a low chockstone close to the ground.

review.notes: Cone page gives how it is reached; route page gives the start. No descent stated.

set.approach: Index is a granite spire in the Five Fingers, on the Bighorn divide in the Cloud Peak Wilderness, south of the Thumb. Hike in from the east (through Highland Park, passing Spear Lake on the way to Loomis Lake) or from the west (starting at Lower Paintrock Lake and crossing the Cliff Lakes country). The route begins at the foot of the orange-coloured east ridge.
set.descent_text: From the summit, downclimb north, then rappel past a large ledge into the talus-filled descent gully.

review.notes: Route page: start and descent; Five Fingers page: both hiking approaches. Rope length left out.
